description: You can extend a compiler with an instruction log and per-operation ranges.

steps.description: The node classes supply expression data. Bytecode records an operation and arguments, while Visitor dispatches by node class.
BytecodeCompiler appends instructions while visiting children. The example binds x to 3 and compiles multiplication nested inside addition.
TracingCompiler records the current instruction count and opcode before each emission. Despite the surrounding source-map discussion, these entries contain operations rather than source lines.

steps.answer: It records the next index before appending, which becomes the new instruction's index.
steps.question: Will the recorded index refer to the instruction before or after it is appended?

steps.description: The subclass also prints each binary node's emitted range. The recording places multiplication at 2..4 and its enclosing addition at 2..6.

title: Trace emitted instruction positions
